title: Inflight coalescer scheduling causes KV-index displacement and softmax perturbation
creator: Daniel Kim
description: Enablement of the inflight coalescer (merge-small-decodes) reduced tail latency and GPU fragmentation but triggered a correctness regression: intermittent softmax output drift and token-rank shuffling in long-context decoder flows. The failure mode is low-rate (~0.3% under stress) but reproducible with a specific concurrency pattern where coalescer flush boundaries coincide with a kernel selection change mid-request. The problem manifests as subtle FP differences that accumulate and occasionally change top-k tokens for later decode steps.
reproduction_steps: 1) Checkout runtime branch inflight-coalescer/enable (PR 12987) and build docker image
2) Start serving with inflight_coalescer=true and coalescer_flush_threshold=4ms
3) Use model rwd-3b-decoder with context length 4096 and 8 concurrent small-decode streams (1-4 tokens per step), deterministic prompt set available in Confluence
4) Run 10k decode iterations under synthetic load; inspect top-5 token distributions per step and compare against baseline without coalescer
5) Observe rare sequences where token ranks diverge starting at step ~120-350 and softmax outputs show percent-level difference compared to baseline
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: race between coalescer flush and KV-slot rotation leading to stale pointer being used by decode kernels

Found cases where a coalescer flush merged requests A and B, triggering a fast-path fused-kernel selection for the merged batch; later a fallback to tiling-kernel occurred for subsequent tokens causing different accumulation order
Numeric traces show sub-ulp differences in softmax inputs immediately after the flush boundary, which amplify under repeated decoding steps
Concurrent KV index updates were observed without explicit ordering barriers when inflight coalescer changes the request-to-buffer mapping
Reproduced the effect deterministically by forcing a kernel-switch at flush boundary using scheduler override flags
root_cause: Race between inflight coalescer flush boundaries and kernel selection logic: the coalescer changes request grouping which can switch kernel/tiling/precision heuristics mid-stream without synchronizing KV index updates. This permits a decode kernel to read an out-of-date KV slot pointer/offset under certain timing windows, producing slightly different accumulators and eventually token-rank divergence.
mitigation: Disable inflight coalescer by default for models with long decode horizons until a fix is deployed
Introduce an ordering barrier in the coalescer flush path that serializes KV-index publication before any kernel selection that may read them
Add a conservative kernel-selection guard: if a flush boundary occurred recently for a given stream, prefer the same kernel family for the next N decode steps
Backfill unit/regression tests that simulate flush-aligned kernel switches and assert top-k token stability against baseline
rollout_plan: Hotfix branch: coalescer/kv-barrier (PR 13012) contains ordering barrier and guard; run e2e rollout to staging
Staging validation: run 1M synthetic decodes across rwd-3b and rwd-7b with diverse concurrency patterns for 48 hours
Gradual rollout: enable coalescer on 10% of hosts, monitor softmax-drift alerting for 72h, then 50% then 100%
Rollback plan: toggle feature-flag inflight_coalescer=false to revert immediately
test_plan: Add deterministic fuzz harness that seeds scheduler timings and forces coalescer flush boundaries at varied offsets
Golden-file regression: record top-10 token distributions for canonical prompts and assert bitwise match for first 256 tokens under high concurrency
Performance regression check: ensure latency/tail improvements remain within 90% of prior gains when ordering barrier is enabled
notes: PM and SRE contacted; SLO alert thresholds temporarily relaxed for affected queues
Affects customers running deterministic evals and RLHF loops; outreach list compiled
Follow-on work: evaluate KV-slot versioning and immutable read snapshots as longer term solution
